depth_findings.text: The purge verifies only the rows it is about to delete, linked to the newest signed checkpoint. It does not check that the head or the newest attested sequence still agree with the retained suffix, so a tampered retained row is caught only by S4's verifier, not by purge.

Attestations are never pruned and the attestor writes one per head change per org. On a hot org that is a row per interval at most. S4 or S9 should decide a retention rule (keep the newest per day) before the table grows.

The purge detects a tampered prefix but does not alert on it: there is no purge, incident or attestation metric (internal/metrics is not owned here), and S4 owns the rules. Add audit_core_chain_purge_blocked_total and an incident-count alert, or the incident table is only visible by querying it.

Replicas each run Attest and Purge. Attest is idempotent via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. A purge that loses the advisory lock skips that org until the next daily sweep, so a purger that stalls leaves expired rows for a day.

Checkpoint signatures cover created_at at microsecond precision, written by the Go side and stored verbatim. S4's verifier and the offline audit-verify CLI must format it with chain.SignedTimeLayout in UTC or every checkpoint will look invalid.

No test covers a purge whose first remaining row links to a checkpoint hash that was altered together with a re-signed checkpoint (attacker holds the key). That is the DB-owner plus key-theft case honest-limits must state.

No test covers the unchained, catch-up-pending expired rows (chain_seq NULL with ingested_at >= activated_at) that Purge deletes by ingested_at before CatchUp chains them. This is pre-existing behaviour from S2 and is not changed here.

The erasure hook (DEC-35 D8) is design only: checkpoint reason 'erasure' is allowed by the migration's CHECK but no code path writes it. A purge-through-head entry point is still needed when the erasure flow lands.
The public key is not served anywhere yet (S5's GET /keys). Until then the AUDIT_CHAIN_PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64 value in the secrets store is the only copy outside the process.

run-control-plane.sh persists the key id, private and public halves independently via persist_if_missing, so a store holding only one half would mint a mismatched pair. The Space-decision block has the same trait. audit-core refuses to boot on a mismatched public key, so it is safe but noisy.

results.notes:
Status is partial because the purge, checkpoint and attestation behaviour is only proven by Postgres tests I could not run (no Postgres here, docker is forbidden). They compile and vet clean but have never executed, so expect to fix the first run.

What was built:
- chain/sign.go: Ed25519 key ring. It accepts base64url and standard base64, padded or not, for a 32-byte seed or a 64-byte key (Appendix B K2-9). It holds an active key plus VerifyKeys (retired public keys, "id:pub,id2:pub"), and has sign and verify for attestations and checkpoints.
- Migration 008 (number reserved in 4.4) adds audit_chain_checkpoints, audit_chain_attestations and audit_chain_incidents, with a revert file. It is additive and embedded in migrate.go.
- store/attest.go has the work in three parts:
  - Attest signs the head of each org chain whose state is ok and not yet attested at that sequence.
  - The chain-safe purge works per org, one 5000-row batch per transaction. It takes pg_try_advisory_xact_lock, finds X = min(chain_seq with ingested_at >= cutoff) - 1 (or the max chain_seq when all rows are expired), verifies the signed checkpoint, and recomputes every row in the batch. Only then does it delete under the maintenance GUC and insert a signed checkpoint in the same transaction. On any verification failure it deletes nothing and writes an incident from the pool. The incident kinds are: chain_marked_broken, checkpoint_key_unknown, checkpoint_signature_invalid, sequence_gap, prev_hash_mismatch, row_hash_mismatch, unsupported_chain_version, unhashable_row, checkpoint_link_mismatch.
  - PruneOff / PruneDryRun / PruneOn modes. Dry run verifies and logs the plan without deleting or writing a checkpoint.
- store.go: Purge calls purgeChained last, and returns the partial result together with any chained-purge error. PurgeResult gains CheckpointsWritten, OrgsBlocked and ChainedPlanned (an addition beyond the plan). Unchained rows still purge by ingested_at.
- main.go:
  - Key loading happens only when the chain or pruning is on; with everything off the key variables are never read.
  - Boot fails on an undecodable key, on a public key that does not match the private key, on prune on without a signing key, and on chain on with ENVIRONMENT=production without a signing key.
  - runAttestor signs heads every AUDIT_CHAIN_ATTEST_INTERVAL (default 60s).
- run-control-plane.sh mints AUDIT_CHAIN_KEY_ID, AUDIT_CHAIN_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64 and AUDIT_CHAIN_PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64 once, as base64url, like the Space-decision pair. validate-release-credentials.sh requires them only when the chain or pruning is on. .env.example lists the variables with prune at 0 and no key values.

Every new switch defaults off. With the chain and prune switches off, behaviour is byte-identical to before.

results.notes:
Built to the plan row with no new switch; the payload and API changes are additive only.

- **Gateway:** `cache_telemetry.rs` is an advisory per-replica classifier.
  - Its state is an in-memory LRU of 4096 threads keyed by a blake3 hash of org, thread and model.
  - A baseline is only a 16-byte blake3 digest of the leading system messages, plus a timestamp.
  - The five reasons are `below_minimum`, `prefix_changed`, `ttl_expired` (idle over 300 s), `no_baseline` and `unexplained`.
  - The minimum-prefix table is a local copy of inference-core's.
  - ZDR turns are never observed (no digest is taken). Subscription turns get no reason.
  - `sse.rs` adds `cache_miss_reason` to the usage envelope payload only when classified, at the streaming site and at `run_infer_fallback`. The `build_usage_envelope` signature is unchanged, so its existing test calls still compile.
- **cost-core:**
  - Migration 0011 adds the nullable `cache_miss_reason` column (idempotent, with a revert file).
  - `Entry.CacheMissReason` is a closed set, validated at the ledger. The NATS decoder drops an unknown value to empty instead of losing the tokens.
  - `UsageBucket` gains cache-read, cache-write and `cache_reported_input_tokens`.
    - `cache_reported_input_tokens` is the hit-rate denominator: the input tokens of turns with a read, a write, or a classified miss other than `below_minimum`.
    - Subscription turns are excluded from all three.
    - Hit rate is read divided by reported.
  - A new `CacheMissAnalytics` read, in memory and in Postgres, returns miss counts per day, model, provider and reason. The `/api/v1/cost/analytics` response carries them as `data.cache_breakdown = {miss_reasons, advisory: true}`.
  - The Go files are CRLF and were kept that way; the new SQL files are LF.
- **Frontend:**
  - `cost-client.ts` adds zod defaults for the new fields.
  - `usage-analytics.ts` adds `cacheHitRate`, `cachePercent`, `cacheMissTotals` and three CSV columns.
  - `UsageAnalyticsSection.tsx` adds a hit-rate tile, a "No cache activity reported" note, a miss-reason line, and a per-row cache-hit column. It reuses existing CSS classes because the CSS file is not owned.
